name: time_machine_status
summary: Report on Time Machine: whether a backup is running right now (and its progress) and when the most recent completed backup was. Use for 'is Time Machine backing up / when did my Mac last back up'. Read-only; runs `tmutil status` and `tmutil latestbackup` and never starts, stops, or deletes a backup.

name: list_backups
summary: List the Time Machine backups available to restore from — both the full snapshots on the backup disk (`tmutil listbackups`) and the local hourly snapshots kept on the startup disk (`tmutil listlocalsnapshots /`). Use for 'what backups do I have / which restore points exist'. Read-only; never creates, deletes, or restores a backup.

name: list_volumes
summary: List every disk and volume attached to this Mac — internal drives, external drives, and mounted disk images — with their identifiers, sizes, and mount points, as `diskutil list` reports them. Use for 'what drives/volumes are connected / what is disk2'. Read-only; runs diskutil only in its listing mode and changes nothing.

name: volume_info
summary: Show detailed information about a single disk or volume — its name, filesystem, size, free space, mount point, and whether it is removable — via `diskutil info`. Use for 'how much space is on my external drive / what filesystem is disk2s1'. Read-only; diskutil is invoked only with its read-only `info` verb.

params.name: volume
params.description: A disk identifier (e.g. disk2 or disk2s1) or a mount path (e.g. /Volumes/Backup). Must not begin with '-'.

name: mount_volume
summary: Mount a disk or volume that is attached but not currently mounted, so its files become accessible under /Volumes, via `diskutil mount`. Use for 'mount disk2s1 / bring my external drive online'. This changes system state (a new volume appears), so it is STAGED for confirmation. It is not auto-undone: to unmount afterwards, the result gives you the exact `diskutil unmount` command to run yourself.

params.name: volume
params.description: The volume to mount: a disk identifier (e.g. disk2s1) or a mount path (e.g. /Volumes/Backup). A disk identifier is the usual choice for a volume that is attached but not yet mounted. Must not begin with '-'.

name: attach_disk_image
summary: Attach (open) a disk image file — a .dmg or .iso — so its contents mount as a volume under /Volumes, via `hdiutil attach`. Use for 'open this dmg / mount the installer image'. This changes system state (a new volume appears), so it is STAGED for confirmation. It is not auto-undone: use the separate detach_disk_image operation (or eject the mounted volume) to close it.

params.name: path
params.description: The disk image file to attach, e.g. ~/Downloads/app.dmg. Must exist and must not begin with '-' (use ./).

name: detach_disk_image
summary: Detach (close) a mounted disk image, unmounting the volume it provided, via `hdiutil detach`. Use for 'close the dmg I opened / unmount this disk image'. Detaching a virtual disk image is benign, but it still changes system state (a volume disappears), so it is STAGED for confirmation. It cannot be auto-undone; re-attach with attach_disk_image if needed.

params.name: mountpoint
params.description: The mount path of the attached image (e.g. /Volumes/Installer) or its disk identifier (e.g. disk4). Must not begin with '-'.

name: eject_volume
summary: Prepare to safely eject a removable disk or volume. This operation NEVER ejects anything itself: it confirms the volume exists, then returns the exact `diskutil eject` command for YOU to run, along with a warning about the consequences. Use for 'eject my external drive / safely remove this disk' — the model hands you the command rather than pulling the disk out from under any app that may be using it.

params.name: volume
params.description: A disk identifier (e.g. disk2) or a mount path (e.g. /Volumes/Backup) of the volume you want to eject. Must not begin with '-'.
